That transmission constraint should cap further near-term hikes even while the inflation gauge remains hot, so the October AONIA contract that already prices a 21.5bp move from overnight AONIA should reprice lower at the next RBA decision and housing/CPI prints.

The Oct-26 contract jumps to 4.565 (+21.5bp) with 4450 volume, then Nov 4.685 (+33.5bp) and Dec 4.725 (+37.5bp); policy-path terminal is Mar-2027 at 4.86 (+51bp). context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known: AU inflation gauge 82 and a global energy shock (WTI 107.02, Brent 130.80, 15-Sep-2026) that already justify some additional RBA tightening, which is why Oct-Dec AONIA prices 21.5-37.5bp of hikes. New as-of 16-Sep-2026: NSW stamp-duty receipts down 24% YoY, volumes down 18%, Sydney and Melbourne values more than 7% below peak — evidence the tightening channel is biting now, not in prospect. That housing print is the information that should change the next meeting, not a restatement of the 82 inflation score.

That path treats inflation/energy as still dominant over housing transmission.
